God grieves over Judah's empty religion: "Come now, let us reason together: though your sins are like scarlet, they shall be as white as snow" (1:18). God's offer is cleansing, not condemnation.
All nations will stream to the mountain of the Lord, and swords will be beaten into ploughshares. A vision of Christ's peace.
Judah's leaders fail; the Lord stands up to judge for the poor. God defends the oppressed.
The Branch of the Lord will be beautiful and glorious; a canopy of glory will cover Zion. Jesus is the Branch.
The song of the vineyard that yielded wild grapes. Jesus told a similar parable; he is the true vine (John 15).
Isaiah sees the Lord high and lifted up and cries "Woe is me". A coal from the altar touches his lips: "Your guilt is taken away" (6:7). Cleansing came from the altar, a picture of the cross.
"The virgin shall conceive and bear a son, and shall call his name Immanuel" (7:14). God with us: Jesus (Matthew 1:23).
God is a sanctuary, but a stone of stumbling for those who reject him (8:14). Jesus is that stone (1 Peter 2:8).
"For to us a child is born, to us a son is given… Wonderful Counsellor, Mighty God, Everlasting Father, Prince of Peace" (9:6). The light shines on those in darkness.
Assyria is a tool that God will judge for its pride. A remnant will return. God's grace keeps a remnant.
A shoot from the stump of Jesse, on whom the Spirit rests; the wolf will lie down with the lamb. Jesus is this Spirit-filled King.
"With joy you will draw water from the wells of salvation" (12:3). God is my salvation; I will trust and not be afraid.
The oracle against Babylon. Proud empires fall; God's kingdom endures.
The fall of the king of Babylon, "Lucifer, son of the morning" (14:12). Pride brought down; Jesus defeated the enemy at the cross.
A lament for Moab. God's heart grieves even over enemy nations.
"A throne will be established in steadfast love" (16:5), a king from David's tent. Fulfilled in Jesus.
Damascus will fall. "You have forgotten the God of your salvation" (17:10). Remember the Rock.
An oracle concerning Cush, which will bring gifts to the Lord. The nations will come to God.
Egypt will be struck and healed, and will know the Lord: "Blessed be Egypt my people" (19:25). God's plan includes every nation.
Isaiah walks barefoot as a sign. Trusting in Egypt instead of God leads to shame.
Babylon is fallen. "Watchman, what of the night?" Morning comes after the night.
The valley of vision. Eliakim is given the key of David (22:22); Jesus holds the key of David (Revelation 3:7).
Tyre's pride brought low. God humbles the proud and blesses the humble.
The earth is laid waste because of broken covenants. Under the new covenant Jesus restores all things.
"He will swallow up death forever; the Lord God will wipe away tears from all faces" (25:8). Fulfilled in Christ (1 Corinthians 15:54).
"You will keep him in perfect peace whose mind is stayed on you" (26:3). The dead will rise (26:19).
God sings over his vineyard and protects it. He will gather his people one by one.
"Behold, I lay in Zion a tested stone, a precious cornerstone; whoever believes will not be ashamed" (28:16). Jesus is that stone (Romans 9:33).
"This people honours me with their lips, but their hearts are far from me" (29:13). Jesus quoted this against empty religion.
"In returning and rest you shall be saved; in quietness and trust shall be your strength" (30:15). The Lord waits to be gracious to you (30:18).
Woe to those who trust in Egypt's horses rather than the Holy One. Trust in God, not human strength.
A king will reign in righteousness, and the Spirit will be poured out from on high. The fruit of righteousness is peace.
"The Lord is our judge, our lawgiver, our king; he will save us" (33:22). No one will say "I am sick" (33:24).
Judgement on the nations. God's justice is real; believers are delivered from wrath through Jesus.
"Strengthen the weak hands… say to the fearful, Be strong, fear not! Your God will come and save you. Then the eyes of the blind shall be opened" (35:3-5). Jesus did exactly this.
Sennacherib's officer mocks Hezekiah's trust in God. The enemy always tries to undermine our trust.
Hezekiah spreads the letter before the Lord, and God destroys the Assyrian army. Bring every threat to God.
Hezekiah is healed and given fifteen more years. God hears prayer and heals.
Hezekiah shows his treasures to Babylon's envoys. Pride in our possessions opens doors to trouble.
"Comfort, comfort my people… her iniquity is pardoned" (40:1-2). "Those who wait on the Lord shall renew their strength" (40:31).
"Fear not, for I am with you; be not dismayed, for I am your God" (41:10).
The Servant of the Lord: "A bruised reed he will not break" (42:3). Jesus is gentle with the broken (Matthew 12:18-21).
"Fear not, for I have redeemed you; I have called you by name; you are mine" (43:1). "I am he who blots out your transgressions… and I will not remember your sins" (43:25).
"I will pour out my Spirit on your offspring" (44:3). Idols are nothing; "I have blotted out your transgressions like a cloud; return to me, for I have redeemed you" (44:22).
God calls Cyrus by name. "Look to me and be saved, all the ends of the earth" (45:22). Every knee will bow (Philippians 2:10).
Idols must be carried, but God carries his people from birth to old age (46:4). Grace carries us.
Proud Babylon will fall. God alone is the Saviour.
"I have refined you in the furnace of affliction". God's grace is for his name's sake; he will not give his glory to another.
"Can a mother forget her nursing child? Even these may forget, yet I will not forget you. I have engraved you on the palms of my hands" (49:15-16).
The Servant gave his back to those who struck him (50:6), fulfilled in Jesus' suffering. He trusts God to vindicate him.
"Look to the rock from which you were hewn". God's salvation is forever; the ransomed of the Lord will return with singing.
"How beautiful are the feet of those who bring good news" (52:7). The Servant will be lifted up, his appearance marred beyond human likeness (52:14).
The suffering Servant: "Surely he has borne our griefs and carried our sorrows… by his stripes we are healed" (53:4-5). The clearest prophecy of the cross: Jesus took our sin and sickness.

"For a brief moment I forsook you, but with great compassion I will gather you" (54:7). As I swore not to flood the earth, "so I have sworn that I will not be angry with you" (54:9). This follows Isaiah 53: wrath was spent on Jesus.
"Come, everyone who thirsts, come to the waters; and he who has no money, come, buy and eat" (55:1). Grace is free. God's word will not return empty.
Foreigners and eunuchs are welcomed into God's house, "a house of prayer for all peoples" (56:7). No outsider is excluded in Christ.
God dwells with the contrite and lowly to revive them (57:15). "Peace, peace to the far and to the near" (57:19).
The fast God chooses: loosing chains, freeing the oppressed, feeding the hungry. "Then your healing shall spring forth speedily" (58:8).
Sin separated us from God, so God himself brought salvation: "his own arm brought him salvation" (59:16). The Redeemer comes to Zion.
"Arise, shine, for your light has come, and the glory of the Lord has risen upon you" (60:1).
"The Spirit of the Lord is upon me… to proclaim good news to the poor, liberty to the captives" (61:1). Jesus read this in Nazareth and said "Today this is fulfilled" (Luke 4:21). Beauty for ashes.
"You shall be called by a new name… my delight is in her" (62:2-4). God rejoices over his people like a bridegroom.
The one in red garments who trod the winepress alone. "In all their affliction he was afflicted" (63:9). God shares our pain.
"All our righteousnesses are like filthy rags" (64:6). We are the clay; God is the potter. Our own works cannot save; only his can.
"Before they call I will answer" (65:24). God creates new heavens and a new earth where weeping is no more.
"As one whom his mother comforts, so I will comfort you" (66:13). God looks to the humble and contrite. All nations will see his glory.
